tools.name: travel_times
tools.description: Counts 1 request per point, whatever the modes; a batch needs a key. Minutes to the nearest place of each amenity type by each mode asked, with basis (block or hexagon) and links.map. points answers a batch in rows, failed points in errors. Next: nearby_places for names, get_catalog for types and co

tools.name: nearby_places
tools.description: Counts 1 request. By default for each of the eight everyday trips: the nearest place on foot with walking minutes, compass direction and whether within the trip's limit, then up to two more within 30 minutes. types may also ask school, elementary_school, secondary_school, childcare, playground or ho

tools.name: walking_routes
tools.description: Needs a key; counts 1 request per type. The walked path to the nearest place of 1–5 types, routed live in the routed cities: a GeoJSON line per type with minutes, metres and seconds at each vertex; types without one are in missing with a reason. Only when the path itself is needed. Next: travel_time

tools.name: check_trip
tools.description: Reach: needs a member's key; counts 1 of 50 Reach answers a day. Whether a trip fits between depart and arrive: spare_minutes or short_minutes; by transit, on how many of 7 departures (3 min apart, depart ± 9 min) it fits, and the worst. stop: when to be there; stop_types: the roomiest places to sto

tools.name: reach_area
tools.description: Reach: needs a member's key; counts 1 of 50 Reach answers a day. The area within minutes of a point by each mode: km², how many places of each type it holds, and the nearest few by name; by transit, typical (most of 7 departures) and worst case. Next: check_trip to test one trip.

tools.name: find_meeting_area
tools.description: Reach: needs a member's key; counts 1 of 50 Reach answers a day. Where everyone, each by their own mode between depart and arrive, could be together at least together_minutes: whether they can, the longest time together, km², and the best places of each type with their shared window. tools.name: find_place
tools.description: Counts 1 request. Up to five towns by name, each with its centre lat and lon, prov and population. Neighbourhoods and suburbs (Kanata, Orléans in Ottawa) are not towns here, and a similar name may be a town elsewhere, so check prov. With lat, lon and a key: places of that name within walk_budget on

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Free, not counted. Types with English and French labels, modes and where each works, periods, statistics, reason codes, what needs a key, coverage (with Reach's), the method and the data version; also the aportee:// resources. Next: travel_times.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Free, not counted. This connection's tier, daily limit and requests left, key_unlocks, free_without_key, and reach (allowed, remaining, or why not). Next: start_sign_in when a key is needed.

tools.name: start_sign_in
tools.description: Free, not counted. A sign-in the person approves in their browser: show them verification_url_complete and user_code (valid expires_in seconds). The key is a free member's key: a higher daily limit and every keyed feature (account_status lists them), Reach included. Next: check_sign_in with device_c

tools.name: check_sign_in
tools.description: Free, not counted. status: pending (ask again after interval), slow_down, denied, expired, or approved with api_key, shown once (then already_issued). Next: repeat the call that needed a key, with api_key as its api_key argument.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "check_sign_in" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
